items.definition:
To supply water to land or crops to aid growth.
Farmers irrigate their fields during dry seasons.

to eat something very quickly and noisily
The hungry dog gobbled down its food.

to say or write something in a different way
Could you please rephrase that question?

give a brief statement of the main points of something
Can you summarise the main points of the report?

to put handcuffs on; to strike with an open hand
The police cuffed the suspect and led him away.

to make a harsh, scraping sound
The old wooden floorboards would creak with every step.

to play better than an opponent
Our team managed to outplay the champions in the final match.

to look at someone or something with one's eyes partly closed
He had to squint to read the small print.

to move quickly
Can you scoot over a bit so I can sit down?

to improve; to surpass
He tried to better his previous performance.

to soak food in a marinade
You should marinate the chicken for at least an hour before grilling.

to replenish a supply of something
We need to restock the shelves before the store opens.

to lie in the sun
She loves to sunbathe on the beach during her holidays.

install again
I had to reinstall the software after the update failed.

to write or draw carelessly or hurriedly
He quickly scribbled a note before leaving.

spin quickly and lightly
She loved to twirl in her new dress.

to vomit
The motion sickness made him want to barf.

to make something less dry
Remember to moisturize your skin daily.

to place in a particular category
Please categorise these documents by date.

to make or become fat
Farmers often fatten their livestock before selling them for meat.

to become ripe; to mature
The apples need a few more days to ripen on the tree.

to make a gesture with the hand, arm, or head to encourage someone to come nearer or follow
She beckoned to him from across the room.

to remove an obstruction from
We need to unblock the drain.

to feel or express sympathy
I sympathise with your situation.

to paint something again
We decided to repaint the living room a lighter color.

to stand, sit, or walk with a drooping posture
Don't slouch; stand up straight!

to move lightly and quickly up and down or from side to side
The jelly began to jiggle when she touched it.

to behave badly
The children were warned not to misbehave during the school trip.

eat too much
It's easy to overeat during the holidays.

apply again
You need to reapply for the visa next year.

settle again or in a different place
Many refugees had to resettle in new countries.

to swim using a snorkel
We went snorkeling in the clear blue waters.

To officially register as a member of an institution or a student on a course.
You need to enrol for the course by Friday.

Cook (food) for too long.
Be careful not to overcook the pasta, or it will be mushy.

sleep lightly
He began to doze off during the long lecture.

to travel by getting free rides from passing vehicles
They decided to hitchhike across the country during their gap year.

to walk quietly on the balls of one's feet
He had to tiptoe past the sleeping baby.

to make modern
They plan to modernise the old factory.

to play a stringed instrument by sweeping the fingers or a plectrum across the strings
He likes to strum his guitar by the campfire.

to mix socially
It's important for children to socialise with their peers.

make small movements, especially of the hands and feet, through nervousness or impatience
The child began to fidget in his seat during the long lecture.

manage badly or inefficiently
The company's finances were severely mismanaged.

make equal or uniform
The team managed to equalize the score in the last minute.

to work (dough or clay) with the hands
She began to knead the dough for bread.

to try again
If the first attempt fails, you can always retry.

to remove the wrapping from
He carefully began to unwrap the present.

to open a zipper
Please unzip your jacket, it's warm in here.

to clean (something) with a disinfectant in order to destroy bacteria
You should disinfect the wound to prevent infection.
